question: Do edits shaped by the activation covariance (Σv) act more than the lens's own directions (v)?
why: Chosen by the human (Zach, 2026-10-15) after exp04's fresh replication; run while the step-direction script is written.

sigma.estimate: population covariance of block outputs over positions 1.. of each window

matched.items: exp02's probe_swap items, eligible as in matched_v4 (stripped prompts, criterion C)
matched.jpart_matched_sigma: per entity and layer: the J-part's cosine to the probe, the rest a seeded draw from N(0, Σ_l) projected orthogonal to the probe
matched.nulls: each condition's matched-norm random-direction null, as exp02

steer.eligibility: as exp03's fresh_steer: answered correctly, with exp03's X and S'
steer.direction: unit(Σ_λ,l (v_S' - v_S)) per layer, v unit lens vectors; Σ_λ = (1 - λ) Σ + λ (tr Σ / d) I
steer.nulls: one seeded random direction per lens and scale, at the same size

decision.matched: fixed before the run: if jpart - jpart_matched_sigma's paired CI includes 0, the matched-control gap is attributed to how natural the direction is; if jpart_matched_sigma - jpart_matched's CI includes 0 and jpart - jpart_matched_sigma's is above 0, to the lens's direction; otherwise reported as mixed. J++ primary, J-lens secondary
decision.steer: Σ-aware writing helps if, for J++ at 3% (the primary dose), some λ < 1 reaches f(f(S')) more often than λ = 1 (paired bootstrap CI above 0); 5% and the J-lens are secondary
decision.reproduce: jpart and jpart_matched must match matched_v4, and λ = 1 must match exp03 fresh_steer, item for item (reported, not fixed)

deviations: Σ comes from WikiText, not from the items' own prompts: it describes generic text, as the lens's Jacobians do.
At λ < 1 the same Euclidean size moves the lens readings less; the test asks whether the shape of the edit matters more than its reading.
